subject: Physics
questionText:
Match the photoelectric effect relations in Column I with their mathematical formulas in Column II (incident photon frequency ν, threshold frequency ν₀, stopping potential V₀, maximum kinetic energy K_max):
Column I:
(A) Einstein's photoelectric equation
(B) Stopping potential relation
(C) de Broglie wavelength of electron accelerated through V volts
(D) Photon momentum (p)
Column II:
(1) K_max = hν - hν₀ = h(ν - ν₀)
(2) e V₀ = K_max
(3) λ = h / √(2m e V) ≈ 1.227 / √V nm
(4) p = h / λ = hν / c
explanation: Einstein's equation: K_max = hν - Φ₀; stopping potential is related by eV₀ = K_max; de Broglie wavelength for electrons is λ = 1.227/√V nm; photon momentum is p = h/λ = hν/c.

subject: Physics
questionText:
Match the experimental observations in photoelectric effect in Column I with their theoretical explanations in Column II:
Column I:
(A) Instantaneous emission of photoelectrons (delay < 10⁻⁹ s)
(B) Existence of threshold frequency (ν₀)
(C) Saturation current is proportional to incident light intensity
(D) Stopping potential depends on frequency, not intensity
Column II:
(1) One-to-one elastic photon-electron collision
(2) Minimum energy needed to overcome surface barrier work function Φ₀ = hν₀
(3) More photons per second eject more photoelectrons per second
(4) Energy of each photon increases linearly with frequency (E = hν)
explanation: Instantaneous emission proves localized packet (photon); threshold frequency corresponds to minimum work function; intensity = photons/sec; photon energy depends solely on frequency.

subject: Physics
questionText:
Match the particles in Column I with their de Broglie wavelength formulas in Column II (mass m, kinetic energy E, absolute temperature T):
Column I:
(A) Particle of mass m and velocity v
(B) Particle of mass m and kinetic energy E
(C) Gas molecule at absolute temperature T
(D) Electron accelerated from rest across potential difference V
Column II:
(1) λ = h / (m v)
(2) λ = h / √(2m E)
(3) λ = h / √(3m k_B T)
(4) λ = h / √(2m e V)
explanation: de Broglie formula: λ = h/p = h/(mv) = h/√(2mE); for thermal neutrons/molecules with average KE = 3/2 k_B T, λ = h/√(3mk_BT); for accelerated charge q=e, λ = h/√(2meV).

subject: Physics
questionText:
Match the milestones in quantum physics in Column I with the associated scientists in Column II:
Column I:
(A) Verification of wave nature of moving electrons by diffraction
(B) Explanation of photoelectric effect via quantum hypothesis
(C) Hypothesis of matter waves (λ = h/p)
(D) Discovery of electron charge-to-mass ratio (e/m)
Column II:
(1) Davisson and Germer
(2) Albert Einstein
(3) Louis de Broglie
(4) J.J. Thomson
explanation: Davisson & Germer proved electron diffraction using nickel crystal in 1927; Einstein won Nobel prize for photoelectric effect; de Broglie proposed wave-particle duality in 1924; Thomson measured e/m in 1897.

subject: Physics
questionText:
Match the photoelectric quantities in Column I with the parameter they are independent of in Column II:
Column I:
(A) Maximum kinetic energy of photoelectrons
(B) Photoelectric threshold wavelength (λ₀)
(C) Saturation photocurrent
(D) Speed of photon in vacuum
Column II:
(1) Intensity of incident radiation
(2) Intensity and frequency of incident light (depends only on metal)
(3) Frequency of incident radiation (at constant incident photon flux)
(4) Motion of source or frequency of wave
explanation: K_max is independent of intensity; threshold wavelength is an intrinsic metal property; saturation current depends on photon arrival rate; c is an invariant universal constant.

subject: Physics
questionText:
Match the following particles accelerated through potential difference V with their de Broglie wavelength formulas:
Column I:
(A) General particle of mass m, charge q, kinetic energy K
(B) Electron accelerated through potential V (in Volts)
(C) Proton accelerated through potential V
(D) Alpha particle (m = 4m_p, q = 2e) vs Proton at same potential V
Column II:
(1) λ = h / p = h / √(2 m K) = h / √(2 m q V)
(2) λ ≈ 12.27 / √V Å (or 1.227 / √V nm)
(3) λ ≈ 0.286 / √V Å
(4) λ_α / λ_p = 1 / (2√2) = 1 : √8
explanation: Standard de Broglie wavelength relations for charged particles.

subject: Physics
questionText:
Match the following photoelectric effect parameters with their dependencies according to Einstein's photoelectric equation (eV₀ = hν - φ₀):
Column I:
(A) Maximum kinetic energy (K_max) and Stopping potential (V₀)
(B) Photoelectric saturation current (I_sat)
(C) Slope of Stopping Potential (V₀) vs Frequency (ν) graph
(D) Threshold frequency (ν₀) and Work function (φ₀ = hν₀)
Column II:
(1) Depends linearly on frequency ν (for ν > ν₀) and is independent of intensity
(2) Directly proportional to intensity of incident radiation (for ν > ν₀)
(3) h / e (universal constant, independent of metal)
(4) Characteristic property of the photosensitive emitter material
explanation: Key experimental laws of photoelectric emission explained by Einstein.

subject: Physics
questionText:
Match the following scientists with their landmark discoveries in Dual Nature of Radiation & Matter:
Column I:
(A) Albert Einstein (1905)
(B) Louis de Broglie (1924)
(C) C.J. Davisson and L.H. Germer (1927)
(D) Philipp Lenard & Wilhelm Hallwachs
Column II:
(1) Quantum explanation of Photoelectric Effect (E = hν)
(2) Wave-particle duality of matter (λ = h / p)
(3) Experimental verification of electron diffraction by Nickel crystal
(4) Experimental study of photoelectric emission and stopping potential
explanation: Historical milestones in NCERT Ch 11.

subject: Physics
questionText:
Match the following photon properties (for radiation of frequency ν and wavelength λ) with their expressions:
Column I:
(A) Energy (E) of a single photon
(B) Linear momentum (p) of a photon
(C) Rest mass (m₀) and speed of a photon in vacuum
(D) Number of photons (n) emitted per second by monochromatic source of power P
Column II:
(1) E = h ν = h c / λ (≈ 1240 / λ(nm) eV)
(2) p = E / c = h / λ = h ν / c
(3) m₀ = 0 and speed = c
(4) n = P / E = P λ / (h c)
explanation: Fundamental photon properties.

subject: Physics
questionText:
Match the following alkali and common metals with their photoelectric work function behavior:
Column I:
(A) Cesium (Cs)
(B) Platinum (Pt)
(C) Sodium (Na) and Potassium (K)
(D) Copper (Cu), Zinc (Zn), and Cadmium (Cd)
Column II:
(1) Lowest work function (~2.14 eV), responds even to visible light
(2) Highest work function (~5.65 eV), requires deep UV light
(3) Respond to visible light (green/blue/violet)
(4) Respond only to Ultraviolet (UV) radiation
explanation: NCERT Table 11.1 work functions and spectral response of metals.

subject: Physics
questionText:
Assertion (A): Photoelectric effect demonstrates particle nature of light.
Reason (R): Photoelectric emission is instantaneous and threshold frequency exists, which wave theory cannot explain.
options: A is true but R is false
Both A and R are true but R is not correct explanation
Both A and R are true and R is correct explanation of A
A is false but R is true
explanation: Instantaneous collision of single photon with electron proves light behaves as discrete particles (photons).

subject: Physics
questionText:
Assertion (A): The wave theory of light completely failed to explain the photoelectric effect.
Reason (R): According to wave theory, energy distributed continuously over the wavefront should take hours or days to accumulate enough energy in a single electron to overcome work function, contradicting immediate emission.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
explanation: Classical wave theory predicted a significant time lag for an electron to absorb sufficient energy from continuous wavefronts and predicted kinetic energy would depend on wave amplitude (intensity), both refuted by experiments.

subject: Physics
questionText:
Assertion (A): The de Broglie wavelength associated with an ordinary moving cricket ball is not observed in everyday life.
Reason (R): The mass of a macroscopic cricket ball is large, making its de Broglie wavelength (~10⁻³⁴ m) infinitely smaller than any measurable physical aperture or crystal lattice.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
explanation: Because Planck's constant h ≈ 6.63 × 10⁻³⁴ J·s is tiny, for mass m ~ 0.15 kg and v ~ 30 m/s, λ = h/(mv) ~ 10⁻³⁴ m, which is far too minuscule to show observable diffraction.

subject: Physics
questionText:
Assertion (A): The stopping potential for photoelectrons emitted from a photosensitive surface depends only on the frequency of the incident light and nature of the photosensitive material.
Reason (R): Stopping potential V₀ satisfies the relation e V₀ = hν - Φ₀, which contains no dependence on the intensity of the incident radiation.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
explanation: From Einstein's relation, e V₀ = hν - Φ₀. For a given metal, V₀ depends linearly on ν and is independent of intensity.

subject: Physics
questionText:
Assertion (A): In Davisson-Germer experiment, a sharp peak in the scattered electron intensity is observed at an accelerating voltage of 54 V and scattering angle of 50°.
Reason (R): The peak arises due to constructive interference of electron matter waves diffracted from atomic planes of the nickel crystal.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
explanation: The 54 V acceleration corresponds to de Broglie wavelength λ = 1.227/√54 = 0.167 nm. Bragg's diffraction formula 2d sin θ = λ matches this precisely at 50° scattering.

subject: Physics
questionText:
Assertion (A): Photons exert radiation pressure when they strike and reflect from a surface.
Reason (R): Even though photons have zero rest mass, they carry momentum p = hν / c = h / λ, which is transferred to the surface during collisions.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
explanation: Photons carry relativistic momentum p = E/c. Change of momentum per unit time exerts a mechanical force and pressure on reflecting or absorbing targets.

subject: Physics
questionText:
Assertion (A): In the photoelectric effect, if the frequency of incident radiation is less than the threshold frequency (ν < ν₀), no photoelectrons are emitted no matter how high the intensity of light is.
Reason (R): Photoelectric emission is an instantaneous one-photon–one-electron collision process, and a single photon must have energy hν ≥ φ₀ to liberate an electron.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
explanation: In the quantum picture, intensity only increases the number of photons per second, not the energy hν of individual photons.

subject: Physics
questionText:
Assertion (A): Photoelectric emission occurs instantaneously (~10⁻⁹ s) without any measurable time lag as soon as radiation of frequency ν > ν₀ falls on the metal, even when the incident intensity is extremely dim.
Reason (R): According to wave theory, energy is spread uniformly over the wavefront and would take hours at low intensity, whereas in quantum theory a single photon transfers all its energy hν at once to a single electron.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
explanation: Instantaneous emission was a fatal blow to the classical wave theory of photoelectric emission.

subject: Physics
questionText:
Assertion (A): Macroscopic objects like a moving cricket ball (m = 0.15 kg, v = 30 m/s) do not exhibit observable wave-like diffraction effects in daily life.
Reason (R): Because Planck's constant h = 6.63 × 10⁻³⁴ J·s is extremely small and the mass of a cricket ball is large, its de Broglie wavelength (λ = h/mv ≈ 1.5 × 10⁻³⁴ m) is many orders of magnitude smaller than any atomic dimension.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
explanation: Wave nature is observable only when λ is comparable to the dimensions of the interacting system (as for electrons where λ ~ 1 Å).

subject: Physics
questionText:
Assertion (A): If an electron and a proton have the same de Broglie wavelength, the electron has a much greater kinetic energy than the proton.
Reason (R): Kinetic energy is related to de Broglie wavelength by K = p² / (2m) = h² / (2 m λ²); for the same λ, kinetic energy is inversely proportional to mass m.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
explanation: Since m_e << m_p and K = h²/(2mλ²), for equal λ we have K_e / K_p = m_p / m_e ≈ 1836.

subject: Physics
questionText:
Assertion (A): If the intensity of incident monochromatic light (with ν > ν₀) is doubled while keeping its frequency constant, the saturation photoelectric current doubles, but the stopping potential V₀ remains unchanged.
Reason (R): Doubling intensity doubles the number of incident photons per second (doubling emitted photoelectrons per second), while the energy hν of each photon remains unchanged.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
explanation: eV₀ = hν - φ₀ depends only on ν and φ₀, not on intensity I.

subject: Physics
questionText:
Consider the following statements regarding photon characteristics:
Statement I: In interaction of radiation with matter, radiation behaves as if it is made up of particles called photons.
Statement II: Photons are electrically neutral and are deflected by both electric and magnetic fields.
Choose the correct option:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
explanation: Statement I is correct. Statement II is incorrect because photons carry zero electric charge and therefore are NOT deflected by electric or magnetic fields.

subject: Physics
questionText:
Consider the following statements regarding the graph of stopping potential (V₀) versus frequency (ν) of incident light:
Statement I: The slope of the V₀ vs ν graph is universal and equals (h / e) for all photosensitive materials.
Statement II: The intercept on the negative potential axis equals -(Φ₀ / e), where Φ₀ is the work function of the metal.
Choose the correct option:
options: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
explanation: Both statements are correct. Rearranging e V₀ = hν - Φ₀ yields V₀ = (h/e)ν - (Φ₀/e). The slope is h/e (constant for all metals) and intercept is -Φ₀/e.

subject: Physics
questionText:
Consider the following statements regarding alkali metals (Cs, K, Na):
Statement I: Alkali metals like Caesium and Potassium have low work functions and can emit photoelectrons even with visible light.
Statement II: Platinum has the highest work function among metals (~5.65 eV) and requires ultraviolet light for photoemission.
Choose the correct option:
options: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
explanation: Both statements are correct NCERT facts. Caesium has the lowest work function (~2.14 eV) sensitive to visible light; Platinum has the highest (~5.65 eV).

subject: Physics
questionText:
Consider the following statements regarding matter waves:
Statement I: The de Broglie wavelength of a particle is inversely proportional to its linear momentum (λ = h / p).
Statement II: For a charged particle with charge q accelerated from rest through potential difference V, the de Broglie wavelength is directly proportional to √V.
Choose the correct option:
options: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
explanation: Statement I is correct. Statement II is incorrect because λ = h / √(2mqV), which means λ is INVERSELY proportional to √V, not directly proportional.

subject: Physics
questionText:
Consider the following statements regarding the Davisson-Germer experiment:
Statement I: The experiment verified the wave nature of electrons, confirming de Broglie's hypothesis.
Statement II: The diffraction phenomenon observed with electrons is identical to X-ray diffraction from crystal planes.
Choose the correct option:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
explanation: Both statements are correct. Electron waves obey Bragg's diffraction law 2d sin θ = nλ in the exact same manner as electromagnetic X-rays.

subject: Physics
questionText:
Statement I: The graphs of stopping potential (V₀) versus frequency (ν) for different photosensitive metals are parallel straight lines having the exact same slope (h / e).
Statement II: The intercept on the frequency axis gives the threshold frequency ν₀, while the intercept on the potential axis gives -φ₀ / e.
options: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
explanation: From V₀ = (h/e)ν - φ₀/e, slope is h/e (universal) and intercepts are ν₀ and -φ₀/e.

subject: Physics
questionText:
Statement I: In the Davisson and Germer experiment with 54 V electrons scattered by a Nickel target, a strong diffraction peak was observed at a scattering angle of φ = 50°, corresponding to de Broglie wavelength λ = 1.65 Å.
Statement II: The theoretical de Broglie wavelength λ = 12.27 / √54 Å ≈ 1.67 Å matched the Bragg diffraction value, confirming the wave nature of electrons.
options: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
explanation: Both statements describe the famous Davisson-Germer experimental result.

subject: Physics
questionText:
Statement I: All photoelectrons emitted from a metal surface by monochromatic light of frequency ν > ν₀ emerge with the exact same kinetic energy (hν - φ₀).
Statement II: Photoelectrons emerge with a distribution of kinetic energies ranging from zero up to a maximum value K_max = hν - φ₀ because many electrons lose energy in internal collisions before escaping the metal surface.
options: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
explanation: Statement I is false (K_max = hν - φ₀ is the MAXIMUM kinetic energy, for the most loosely bound electrons escaping without internal collision losses). Statement II is true.

subject: Physics
questionText:
Statement I: For a photon of energy E and wavelength λ, its momentum is p = h / λ = E / c, which is the exact same relation between wavelength and momentum (p = h / λ) that holds for matter waves.
Statement II: When the intensity of monochromatic light of a given wavelength is increased, the momentum of each individual photon increases.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
explanation: Statement I is true. Statement II is false: increasing intensity increases the number of photons per second, NOT the momentum h/λ of each photon.

subject: Physics
questionText:
Statement I: The de Broglie wavelength of a thermal neutron at absolute temperature T (having kinetic energy K = 3/2 k_B T) is λ = h / √(3 m_n k_B T).
Statement II: Thermal neutrons have de Broglie wavelengths (~1.4 Å at 300 K) comparable to interatomic spacing in crystals and are widely used for neutron diffraction studies.
options: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
explanation: Both statements are correct.

subject: Physics
questionText: Energy gap (Eg) of a semiconductor is 1.24 eV. Longest wavelength of photon that can excite electron is: (hc = 1240 eV nm)
explanation: λ = hc / Eg = 1240 eV nm / 1.24 eV = 1000 nm.

subject: Physics
questionText: The work function of a metal is 2.0 eV. What is the threshold frequency of radiation for photoelectric emission from this metal? (h = 6.63 × 10⁻³⁴ J·s)
explanation: Work function W = 2.0 eV = 2.0 × 1.6 × 10⁻¹⁹ J = 3.2 × 10⁻¹⁹ J. Threshold frequency ν0 = W/h = (3.2 × 10⁻¹⁹)/(6.63 × 10⁻³⁴) ≈ 4.83 × 10¹⁴ Hz.

subject: Physics
questionText: What is the de Broglie wavelength of an electron accelerated through a potential difference of 100 V?
explanation: Formula for electron de Broglie wavelength λ = 1.227 / √V nm = 1.227 / √100 = 1.227 / 10 = 0.1227 nm ≈ 0.123 nm.

subject: Physics
questionText: Work function of a metal is 4.0 eV. Maximum kinetic energy of photoelectrons emitted by photon of energy 6.0 eV is:
explanation: Einstein's Photoelectric Equation: KE_max = E - W = 6.0 - 4.0 = 2.0 eV.

subject: Physics
questionText: If stopping potential for photoelectrons emitted from a surface is 3 V, maximum kinetic energy of emitted electrons is:
explanation: KE_max = e × V0 = 3.0 eV.

subject: Physics
questionText: Momentum of a photon of wavelength 663 nm is: (h = 6.63 × 10⁻³⁴ J·s)

subject: Physics
questionText: The work function of Caesium is 2.14 eV. When light of frequency 6.0 × 10¹⁴ Hz is incident on the metal surface, what is the maximum kinetic energy of the emitted electrons? (h = 4.14 × 10⁻¹⁵ eV·s)
explanation: Photon energy E = hν = (4.14 × 10⁻¹⁵ eV·s) × (6.0 × 10¹⁴ s⁻¹) = 2.484 eV. Maximum kinetic energy K_max = E - Φ₀ = 2.484 eV - 2.140 eV = 0.344 eV.

subject: Physics
questionText: What is the de Broglie wavelength associated with an electron accelerated through a potential difference of 100 volts?

subject: Physics
questionText: When ultraviolet light of wavelength 200 nm falls on a metal surface, the stopping potential is observed to be 2.5 V. What is the work function of the metal? (hc = 1240 eV·nm)
explanation: Energy of incident photon E = 1240 / 200 = 6.2 eV. Since eV₀ = 2.5 eV, work function Φ₀ = E - eV₀ = 6.2 eV - 2.5 eV = 3.7 eV.

subject: Physics
questionText: An electron, an α-particle, and a proton have the same kinetic energy. Which of these particles has the shortest de Broglie wavelength?
explanation: de Broglie wavelength λ = h / √(2m E). For identical kinetic energy E, λ ∝ 1/√m. Since the α-particle has the largest mass (m_α ≈ 4 m_p ≫ m_e), it has the shortest wavelength.

subject: Physics
questionText: A monochromatic laser of frequency 6 × 10¹⁴ Hz produces power of 2.0 × 10⁻³ W. How many photons per second on average are emitted by the source? (Take h = 6.63 × 10⁻³⁴ J·s)
explanation: Energy per photon E = hν = 6.63 × 10⁻³⁴ × 6 × 10¹⁴ = 3.978 × 10⁻¹⁹ J. Number of photons per second N = P / E = (2.0 × 10⁻³ J/s) / (3.978 × 10⁻¹⁹ J) ≈ 5.03 × 10¹⁵ s⁻¹.

subject: Physics
questionText: What is the de Broglie wavelength associated with an electron accelerated from rest through a potential difference of 100 Volts?

subject: Physics
questionText: Monochromatic light of wavelength 400 nm is incident on a metal whose work function is 2.1 eV (take hc = 1240 eV·nm). The maximum kinetic energy of the emitted photoelectrons and the stopping potential are respectively:
explanation: Photon energy E = 1240 / 400 = 3.1 eV. Thus K_max = E - φ₀ = 3.1 - 2.1 = 1.0 eV, and stopping potential V₀ = 1.0 V.

subject: Physics
questionText: When a metal surface is illuminated with light of wavelength λ, the stopping potential is V₀. When the same surface is illuminated with light of wavelength 2λ, the stopping potential drops to V₀ / 4. The threshold wavelength λ₀ for the metal is:
explanation: eV₀ = hc/λ - hc/λ₀ and eV₀/4 = hc/(2λ) - hc/λ₀. Multiplying the second by 4: hc/λ - hc/λ₀ = 2hc/λ - 4hc/λ₀ => 3hc/λ₀ = hc/λ => λ₀ = 3λ.

subject: Physics
questionText: A monochromatic laser source operating at wavelength 663 nm emits a power of 3.0 mW (take h = 6.63 × 10⁻³⁴ J·s, c = 3 × 10⁸ m/s). The number of photons emitted per second by the laser is:
explanation: Energy of 1 photon E = hc / λ = (6.63 × 10⁻³⁴ × 3 × 10⁸) / (663 × 10⁻⁹) = 3.0 × 10⁻¹⁹ J. Number per second n = P / E = (3.0 × 10⁻³) / (3.0 × 10⁻¹⁹) = 1.0 × 10¹⁶ s⁻¹.

subject: Physics
questionText: If the kinetic energy of a free particle is increased to 16 times its initial value, its de Broglie wavelength becomes:
explanation: Since λ = h / √(2mK) ∝ 1/√K, when K' = 16 K, λ' = λ / √16 = λ / 4.

subject: Physics
questionText: If the momentum of an electron is increased by 100% (doubled), the percentage change in its de Broglie wavelength is:
explanation: λ = h / p. When p' = 2p, λ' = h / (2p) = 0.5 λ, which is a 50% decrease.

subject: Physics
questionText: Photoelectric effect is explained by:
explanation: Einstein explained photoelectric effect using photon concept — KE = hν − φ.

subject: Physics
questionText: de Broglie wavelength of a particle of momentum p is:
explanation: λ = h/p — de Broglie relation.

subject: Physics
questionText: Work function is the minimum energy needed to:
options: Eject an electron from metal surface
Excite an electron to next orbit
explanation: Work function φ = minimum energy to liberate an electron from a metal surface.

subject: Physics
questionText: Energy of a photon of frequency ν is:
explanation: E = hν (Planck's quantum theory of radiation).

subject: Physics
questionText: In Photoelectric Effect, the maximum kinetic energy (K_max = e V0) of emitted photoelectrons depends ONLY on:
options: Frequency (or wavelength) of incident light (and work function of metal), independent of intensity
explanation: Einstein: K_max = hν - Φ0. Increasing frequency increases photoelectron kinetic energy and stopping potential V0; increasing intensity increases photocurrent.

subject: Physics
questionText: Stopping Potential (V0) in photoelectric effect is the minimum negative retarding potential applied to anode at which:
options: Photoelectric current drops to zero (e V0 = K_max = 1/2 m v_max^2)
explanation: Stopping potential V0 stops the most energetic photoelectrons: e V0 = hν - Φ0.

subject: Physics
questionText: The slope of the graph between Stopping Potential (V0) and Incident Frequency (ν) is equal to:
options: h / e (Universal constant independent of target metal)
explanation: V0 = (h/e) ν - (Φ0/e). Slope of V0 vs ν line is h/e = 4.14 × 10⁻¹⁵ V·s.

questionText: Davisson and Germer Experiment (1927) provided direct experimental verification of wave nature of electrons through:
options: Electron diffraction by Nickel crystal lattice (maximum diffraction intensity observed at 54 V and scattering angle 50°)
explanation: Clinton Davisson and Lester Germer observed constructive interference of electron waves scattered from nickel crystals at 54 V (λ = 1.66 Å).

subject: Physics
questionText: Work function (Φ0 = h ν0) of Cesium (Cs) is 2.14 eV, the lowest among all metals, which makes Cesium ideal for:
explanation: Cesium has the lowest work function (2.14 eV) and highest photosensitivity, operating even with visible red light.

explanation: Energy difference E1-E2 is largest for n=2 to n=1 transition.

subject: Physics
questionText: Einstein's Photoelectric Equation is based on conservation of:
explanation: Photon energy hν is split into work function W0 and maximum kinetic energy Kmax.

subject: Physics
questionText: Stopping potential (V0) in photoelectric experiment depends on:
explanation: Stopping potential e V0 = Kmax = hν - W0; depends on frequency ν, independent of intensity.

subject: Physics
questionText: Number of photoelectrons emitted per second (photoelectric current) is directly proportional to:
explanation: Intensity = number of photons per second. Higher intensity emits more photoelectrons per second.

explanation: λ = h / √(2m e V) = 12.27 / √V Angstroms.

subject: Physics
questionText: Minimum frequency of incident radiation below which no photoelectric emission occurs is:
explanation: Below threshold frequency ν0 (where hν0 = W0), no electron emission takes place regardless of intensity.

subject: Physics
questionText: Rest mass of a photon is:
explanation: Photon travels at speed of light c; its rest mass m0 is zero.

subject: Physics
questionText: Momentum of a photon of frequency ν and wavelength λ is:
explanation: Photon energy E = hν = pc => p = hν / c = h / λ.

subject: Physics
questionText: Davisson and Germer experiment provided experimental verification of:
explanation: Electron diffraction from nickel crystal in Davisson-Germer experiment proved de Broglie wave nature of matter.

subject: Physics
questionText: Slope of the graph between Stopping Potential (V0) and Frequency (ν) of incident light equals:
explanation: e V0 = hν - W0 => V0 = (h/e) ν - (W0/e). Slope of V0 vs ν line = h / e.

subject: Physics
questionText: Ratio of de Broglie wavelength of an alpha particle and a proton accelerated through same potential difference V is:
explanation: λ = h / √(2 m q V). m_alpha = 4 m_p, q_alpha = 2 q_p. λ_alpha / λ_p = √(m_p q_p / (4 m_p × 2 q_p)) = 1 / √8 = 1 / (2√2).

subject: Physics
questionText: Mass of photon at rest is:
explanation: Rest mass of a photon is zero.

subject: Physics
questionText: If momentum of a particle is doubled, its de Broglie wavelength becomes:
explanation: λ = h / p. If p' = 2 p, then λ' = λ / 2.

subject: Physics
questionText: A proton and an alpha particle have the SAME kinetic energy K. The ratio of their de Broglie wavelengths (λ_p : λ_α) is:
explanation: For the same kinetic energy K, λ = h / √(2mK) ∝ 1/√m. Since m_α = 4 m_p, λ_p / λ_α = √(4m_p / m_p) = 2 : 1.

subject: Physics
questionText: A stationary nucleus of mass M decays by emitting a gamma-ray photon of momentum p, or splits into two fragments of unequal masses m₁ and m₂ in a two-body decay from rest. For the two daughter fragments m₁ and m₂ flying apart, the ratio of their de Broglie wavelengths (λ₁ : λ₂) is:
explanation: By conservation of linear momentum from rest, |p₁| = |p₂|. Since λ = h / |p|, both fragments have the exact same de Broglie wavelength (λ₁ : λ₂ = 1 : 1)!

subject: Physics
questionText: When monochromatic light of frequency 2 ν₀ (where ν₀ is the threshold frequency) is incident on a metallic plate, the maximum velocity of emitted photoelectrons is v₁. When the frequency is increased to 5 ν₀, the maximum velocity becomes v₂. The ratio v₁ : v₂ is:
explanation: ½ m v₁² = h(2ν₀ - ν₀) = hν₀; and ½ m v₂² = h(5ν₀ - ν₀) = 4hν₀. Thus (v₁/v₂)² = 1/4 => v₁ : v₂ = 1 : 2.

subject: Physics
questionText: Which of the following figures/experiments provides the most direct evidence for the PARTICLE (quantum) nature of light?
options: Polarization of light by Brewster reflection
explanation: Interference, diffraction, and polarization are explained by wave theory, whereas photoelectric effect and Compton effect require photon (particle) quanta.

subject: Physics
questionText: If a point source of light is moved from a distance of 1.0 m to 0.5 m from a photocell (halving the distance r), the stopping potential V₀ and saturation photocurrent I_sat change as follows:
options: Stopping potential V₀ remains unchanged, while saturation current I_sat becomes 4 times
Both V₀ and I_sat become 4 times
V₀ becomes 2 times and I_sat becomes 4 times
V₀ remains unchanged and I_sat becomes 2 times
explanation: For a point source, intensity I ∝ 1/r². Halving r quadruples intensity I (quadrupling I_sat), while frequency ν and hence stopping potential V₀ remain unchanged.

subject: Physics
questionText: A photon and an electron both have the same wavelength λ. Which of the following statements is true regarding their linear momenta?
options: Both have the exact same magnitude of linear momentum (p = h / λ)
explanation: Since p = h / λ applies identically to both photons and matter waves, equal wavelength λ implies equal momentum magnitude p.

subject: Physics
questionText: The slope of the straight-line graph plotted between Maximum Kinetic Energy (K_max) of photoelectrons on the y-axis and Frequency (ν) of incident light on the x-axis is equal to:
explanation: From K_max = h ν - φ₀, the slope d(K_max)/dν is Planck's constant h (whereas the slope of V₀ vs ν is h/e).

subject: Physics
questionText: In an electron microscope, electrons are accelerated through a very high voltage (~50 kV) instead of using visible light because:
options: Glass lenses focus electrons better than magnetic lenses
High-energy electrons have a de Broglie wavelength (~0.05 Å) about 10⁵ times smaller than visible light, giving vastly superior resolving power
explanation: Resolving power of a microscope is inversely proportional to wavelength (RP ∝ 1/λ); tiny electron de Broglie wavelength gives atomic-scale resolution.

subject: Physics
questionText: Two metals A and B have work functions 2 eV and 4 eV respectively. Which metal has a LARGER threshold wavelength (λ₀)?
options: Metal A (with λ₀ = 620 nm vs 310 nm for B)
Both have the same threshold wavelength
explanation: Since φ₀ = hc / λ₀, λ₀ is inversely proportional to φ₀. Metal A (2 eV) has λ₀ = 1240/2 = 620 nm, twice that of Metal B (310 nm).

subject: Physics
questionText: In photoelectric emission, the photoelectric current is directly proportional to:
options: The frequency of incident light only
The number of photoelectrons emitted per second (and intensity of incident light for ν > ν₀)
The work function of the metal
explanation: Photocurrent I = n e, which is proportional to the rate of photoelectron emission and incident photon flux (intensity).

subject: Physics
questionText: If we consider electrons and photons of the same wavelength λ, then they will have the same:
explanation: Both obey p = h/λ, so equal λ means equal linear momentum p, whereas E_photon = pc and E_electron = p²/(2m) are different.

subject: Physics
questionText: When ultraviolet rays are incident on a negatively charged zinc plate connected to a gold-leaf electroscope, the divergence of the gold leaves:
options: Decreases (as photoelectrons are emitted and negative charge is lost)
explanation: Hallwachs observed that UV light causes a negatively charged zinc plate to lose its negative charge by emitting photoelectrons.

subject: Physics
questionText: A plane electromagnetic wave of intensity I = 600 W/m^2 falls normally on a flat surface of area A = 10 cm^2 (10^-3 m^2). Compare the radiation pressure (P_rad) and radiation force (F_rad) exerted on the surface if: (Case I) the surface is a 100% black absorber, versus (Case II) the surface is a 100% perfect mirror reflector: (Speed of light c = 3 × 10^8 m/s)
options: Case I (Absorber): P_rad = I / c = 2 × 10^-6 Pa, F_rad = 2 × 10^-9 N; Case II (Reflector): P_rad = 2I / c = 4 × 10^-6 Pa, F_rad = 4 × 10^-9 N
Case I: P_rad = 2I / c; Case II: P_rad = I / c
Case I: P_rad = I × c; Case II: P_rad = 0
Both absorber and reflector experience identical radiation pressure I / c
explanation: Electromagnetic waves carry momentum p = U / c. For complete absorption (Case I), momentum transferred per second per unit area is P_rad = I / c = 600 / (3 × 10^8) = 2 × 10^-6 N/m^2 (Pa), and Force = P_rad × A = 2 × 10^-9 N. For 100% reflection (Case II), photon momentum reverses (+p to -p, change = 2p), doubling the radiation pressure to P_rad = 2I / c = 4 × 10^-6 Pa!

subject: Physics
questionText: Which particle has zero rest mass?
explanation: Photon is a massless particle, always moving with speed of light.

subject: Physics
questionText: The energy of a photon is given by?
explanation: Photon energy E = hf, where h is Planck’s constant and f is frequency.

subject: Physics
questionText: The work function is the minimum energy required to?
options: Remove an electron from a metal surface
explanation: Work function is the minimum energy needed to liberate an electron from a surface.

subject: Physics
questionText: Photoelectric effect proves the?
explanation: Photoelectric effect shows light behaves as photons (particles).

subject: Physics
questionText: Einstein’s photoelectric equation is?
explanation: Photoelectric equation: hf = φ + KEmax.

subject: Physics
questionText: In photoelectric effect, stopping potential depends on?
explanation: Stopping potential depends on frequency of incident radiation.

subject: Physics
questionText: Which of the following has particle as well as wave nature?
explanation: Light shows wave–particle duality (photoelectric effect + interference).

subject: Physics
questionText: The work function of a metal is 2 eV. Threshold frequency is approximately?
explanation: Threshold frequency f₀ = W/h ≈ 2 eV / 6.63×10⁻³⁴ ≈ 4.8×10¹⁴ Hz.

subject: Physics
questionText: Which particle has no charge and mass nearly equal to proton?
explanation: Neutron is neutral and has mass nearly equal to proton.

subject: Physics
questionText: The de Broglie wavelength is inversely proportional to?
explanation: λ = h/p, and p = mv, so depends on mass and velocity.

subject: Physics
questionText: The threshold frequency depends on?
explanation: Threshold frequency is characteristic of the metal.

subject: Physics
questionText:
Match the spectral series of the hydrogen atom in Column I with their corresponding regions of the electromagnetic spectrum in Column II:
Column I:
(A) Lyman series
(B) Balmer series
(C) Paschen series
(D) Brackett and Pfund series
Column II:
(1) Ultraviolet (UV) region
(2) Visible region (and near UV)
(3) Near Infrared (IR) region
(4) Far Infrared (IR) region
explanation: Lyman series (n₁=1) lies in UV; Balmer series (n₁=2) lies in visible; Paschen (n₁=3) in near IR; Brackett (n₁=4) and Pfund (n₁=5) in far IR.

subject: Physics
questionText:
Match the Bohr model parameters for hydrogen atom in Column I with their dependence on principal quantum number n in Column II:
Column I:
(A) Orbit radius (r_n)
(B) Orbital velocity of electron (v_n)
(C) Total energy of orbit (E_n)
(D) Orbital time period (T_n)
Column II:
(1) Directly proportional to n² (∝ n²)
(2) Inversely proportional to n (∝ 1/n)
(3) Inversely proportional to n² (∝ -1/n²)
(4) Directly proportional to n³ (∝ n³)
explanation: In Bohr atom: r ∝ n²/Z; v ∝ Z/n; E ∝ -Z²/n²; Time period T = 2πr/v ∝ n³ / Z².

subject: Physics
questionText:
Match the nuclear properties in Column I with their mathematical formulas or characteristics in Column II:
Column I:
(A) Nuclear radius (R)
(B) Mass defect (Δm)
(C) Nuclear density
(D) Half-life period (T_1/2)
Column II:
(1) R₀ A^(1/3) where R₀ ≈ 1.2 × 10⁻¹⁵ m
(2) [Z m_p + (A - Z) m_n] - M_nucleus
(3) Constant (~2.3 × 10¹⁷ kg/m³), independent of mass number A
(4) 0.693 / λ
explanation: Nuclear radius R = R₀ A^(1/3); mass defect Δm = [Zm_p + (A-Z)m_n] - M; density ρ = M/V ∝ A / (A^(1/3))³ = const (~10¹⁷ kg/m³); half life T_1/2 = ln(2)/λ.

subject: Physics
questionText:
Match the nuclear processes in Column I with their defining characteristics in Column II:
Column I:
(A) Nuclear Fission
(B) Nuclear Fusion
(C) Alpha (α) decay
(D) Beta-minus (β⁻) decay
Column II:
(1) Heavy nucleus (e.g. U-235) splits into lighter nuclei with energy release
(2) Light nuclei (e.g. hydrogen isotopes) combine at extreme temperature (~10⁷ K)
(3) Nucleus emits Helium nucleus (⁴₂He), mass number decreases by 4, atomic number by 2
(4) A neutron transforms into a proton with emission of electron and antineutrino
explanation: Fission: splitting of heavy nucleus; Fusion: combining of light nuclei; Alpha decay: emits ⁴₂He; β⁻ decay: n → p + e⁻ + ν_bar.

subject: Physics
questionText:
Match the atomic models in Column I with their major limitation or discovery in Column II:
Column I:
(A) Thomson's plum pudding model
(B) Rutherford's planetary model
(C) Bohr's quantum model
(D) Chadwick's experiment
Column II:
(1) Failed to explain large angle alpha particle scattering
(2) Could not explain orbital stability (classical electrodynamics radiates away energy)
(3) Could not explain fine structure and spectra of multi-electron atoms
(4) Discovered neutral constituent of nucleus (neutron)
explanation: Thomson's model failed to account for backward alpha scattering; Rutherford's model predicted continuous spiral collapse; Bohr's model only applies to single-electron species; Chadwick discovered neutron in 1932.

subject: Physics
questionText:
Match the following spectral series of the Hydrogen atom with the lower principal quantum number (n₁) and spectral region:
Column I:
(A) Lyman series
(B) Balmer series
(C) Paschen series
(D) Brackett and Pfund series
Column II:
(1) n₁ = 1, Ultraviolet (UV) region
(2) n₁ = 2, Visible region
(3) n₁ = 3, Near Infrared (IR) region
(4) n₁ = 4 and n₁ = 5, Far Infrared (IR) region
explanation: Standard Hydrogen spectral series from Rydberg formula 1/λ = R(1/n₁² - 1/n₂²).

subject: Physics
questionText:
Match the following Bohr orbit quantities for a hydrogen-like ion (atomic number Z, principal quantum number n) with their dependencies:
Column I:
(A) Radius of nth Bohr orbit (r_n)
(B) Speed of electron in nth Bohr orbit (v_n)
(C) Total energy of electron in nth Bohr orbit (E_n)
(D) Orbital Angular Momentum (L_n) in nth Bohr orbit
Column II:
(1) r_n = 0.529 (n² / Z) Å  [r_n ∝ n² / Z]
(2) v_n = (2.18 × 10⁶ m/s) (Z / n)  [v_n ∝ Z / n]
(3) E_n = -13.6 (Z² / n²) eV  [E_n ∝ Z² / n²]
(4) L_n = n h / (2π)  [independent of Z]
explanation: Standard Bohr atomic model scaling laws.

subject: Physics
questionText:
Match the following nuclear properties and radioactive decay relations with their formulas:
Column I:
(A) Nuclear radius R as a function of mass number A
(B) Nuclear mass density ρ_nuc
(C) Radioactive decay law and Half-life (T_½)
(D) Mean life (τ) and Activity (A = |dN/dt|)
Column II:
(1) R = R₀ A^(1/3) (where R₀ ≈ 1.2 × 10⁻¹⁵ m)
(2) Approximately constant (~2.3 × 10¹⁷ kg/m³), independent of A
(3) N(t) = N₀ e^(-λt) and T_½ = ln(2) / λ = 0.693 / λ
(4) τ = 1 / λ = 1.44 T_½ and Activity R(t) = λ N(t)
explanation: Fundamental nuclear structure and radioactivity formulas.

subject: Physics
questionText:
Match the following types of nuclear transformations with the changes in Atomic Number (Z) and Mass Number (A):
Column I:
(A) Alpha (α) decay (emission of ⁴₂He nucleus)
(B) Beta-minus (β⁻) decay (n → p + e⁻ + ν̄_e)
(C) Beta-plus (β⁺) positron decay (p → n + e⁺ + ν_e)
(D) Gamma (γ) decay (de-excitation of excited nucleus)
Column II:
(1) Z decreases by 2, A decreases by 4
(2) Z increases by 1, A remains unchanged
(3) Z decreases by 1, A remains unchanged
(4) Both Z and A remain unchanged
explanation: Radioactive displacement laws (Soddy-Fajans rules).

subject: Physics
questionText:
Match the following classification of nuclides with their definitions and examples:
Column I:
(A) Isotopes
(B) Isobars
(C) Isotones
(D) Mass Energy equivalence of 1 atomic mass unit (1 u)
Column II:
(1) Same Z, different A (e.g., ¹₁H, ²₁H, ³₁H)
(2) Same A, different Z (e.g., ³₁H and ³₂He; ¹⁴₆C and ¹⁴₇N)
(3) Same neutron number N = A - Z (e.g., ³₁H and ⁴₂He)
(4) 1 u × c² ≈ 931.5 MeV
explanation: Standard definitions of isotopes, isobars, isotones, and mass-energy equivalence.

subject: Physics
questionText:
Assertion (A): Nuclear density is practically constant for all atomic nuclei, regardless of their atomic mass number A.
Reason (R): Nuclear volume is directly proportional to mass number A (V ∝ R³ ∝ A), which exactly cancels out the mass dependence in density = Mass / Volume.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
explanation: Since R = R₀ A^(1/3), Volume V = 4/3 π R₀³ A. Total mass M ≈ m_N A. Therefore density ρ = M/V = m_N / (4/3 π R₀³), which is an absolute constant ~ 2.3 × 10¹⁷ kg/m³.

subject: Physics
questionText:
Assertion (A): Energy is released in both nuclear fission of heavy nuclei and nuclear fusion of light nuclei.
Reason (R): In both processes, the binding energy per nucleon of the resulting daughter nuclei is higher than that of the reactant parent nuclei.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
explanation: The binding energy per nucleon curve peaks around Fe-56 (8.8 MeV/nucleon). Moving towards the peak from both ends (fusing light nuclei or splitting heavy nuclei) increases BE/nucleon, releasing the mass-defect difference as energy.

subject: Physics
questionText:
Assertion (A): Rutherford's alpha particle scattering experiment led to the discovery of the atomic nucleus.
Reason (R): A small fraction (about 1 in 8000) of alpha particles were deflected by more than 90°, showing that the entire positive charge and mass are concentrated in a tiny central region.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
explanation: Large angle rebound of heavy alpha particles could only be produced by a tremendous electrostatic repulsion concentrated in a tiny, massive core (nucleus).

subject: Physics
questionText:
Assertion (A): Nuclear forces are non-central, charge-independent, and exhibit saturation.
Reason (R): The strong nuclear force between a proton-proton, proton-neutron, and neutron-neutron pair is identical inside the nucleus.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
explanation: Nuclear force acts equally between any two nucleons (charge independence). Saturation means each nucleon only interacts with its immediate nearest neighbors.

subject: Physics
questionText:
Assertion (A): Ionization energy of a hydrogen atom in its ground state is 13.6 eV.
Reason (R): The ground state energy of an electron in hydrogen atom is -13.6 eV, so +13.6 eV of energy must be supplied to remove it to infinity.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
explanation: E₁ = -13.6 / 1² = -13.6 eV. Ionization energy is E_∞ - E₁ = 0 - (-13.6) = +13.6 eV.

subject: Physics
questionText:
Assertion (A): The mass density of all atomic nuclei (from light Helium to heavy Uranium) is nearly constant (~2.3 × 10¹⁷ kg/m³) and is independent of mass number A.
Reason (R): The nuclear radius varies as R = R₀ A^(1/3), so the nuclear volume V = (4/3)π R³ = (4/3)π R₀³ A is directly proportional to the nuclear mass (A u), causing A to cancel out in density = Mass / Volume.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
explanation: Because both mass and volume are proportional to A, nuclear density is universal and constant.

subject: Physics
questionText:
Assertion (A): Heavy nuclei with mass number A > 200 undergo nuclear fission, while very light nuclei with A < 20 undergo nuclear fusion, and both processes release huge amounts of energy.
Reason (R): Both fission of heavy nuclei and fusion of light nuclei produce product nuclei in the intermediate mass range (30 < A < 170) where the binding energy per nucleon (E_bn) is higher (peaking at ~8.75 MeV for ⁵⁶Fe).
options: Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
explanation: Any nuclear reaction that moves nucleons from lower binding energy per nucleon to higher binding energy per nucleon releases energy.

subject: Physics
questionText:
Assertion (A): In Rutherford's alpha-particle scattering experiment, the vast majority of alpha particles pass almost straight through the thin gold foil without deflection, while only about 1 in 8000 deflects by more than 90°.
Reason (R): Almost all the mass and all the positive charge of an atom are concentrated in an extremely tiny central nucleus (~10⁻¹⁵ m) compared to the size of the atom (~10⁻¹⁰ m), leaving most of the atom empty space.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
explanation: Rutherford's scattering experiment established the nuclear model of the atom.

subject: Physics
questionText:
Assertion (A): The nuclear force binding protons and neutrons together inside a nucleus is charge-independent.
Reason (R): For a given nucleon separation (~1–2 fm), the attractive strong nuclear force between two protons (p–p), two neutrons (n–n), and a proton and a neutron (p–n) is virtually identical.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
explanation: Strong nuclear force does not depend on electric charge: F_nn ≈ F_pp ≈ F_np.

subject: Physics
questionText:
Assertion (A): The mass of any stable nucleus is always slightly LESS than the sum of the individual rest masses of its constituent free protons and neutrons.
Reason (R): During the formation of a nucleus from free nucleons, the mass defect Δm = [Z m_p + (A - Z) m_n - M_nuc] is released as nuclear binding energy (ΔE_b = Δm c²).
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
explanation: To break the nucleus apart into free nucleons, energy equal to the binding energy Δm c² must be supplied.

subject: Physics
questionText:
Assertion (A): Alpha particles have high ionising power but low penetrating power.
Reason (R): Alpha particles are heavy and have charge +2e.
options: Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.
explanation: Being heavy and highly charged, they interact strongly with matter, ionising it rapidly but losing energy quickly.

subject: Physics
questionText:
Assertion (A): Nuclear density is nearly constant for all nuclei (~2.3 x 10^17 kg/m^3).
Reason (R): Nuclear volume V is directly proportional to mass number A (V ∝ A), canceling out in density = Mass / Volume.
options: A is true but R is false
Both A and R are true but R is not correct explanation
Both A and R are true and R is correct explanation of A
A is false but R is true
explanation: Mass ∝ A and Volume ∝ A => Density = Mass/Volume is constant for all nuclei.

subject: Physics
questionText:
Consider the following statements regarding Bohr's postulates:
Statement I: Electrons revolve only in those non-radiating orbits where their orbital angular momentum is an integral multiple of h / (2π).
Statement II: Radiation is emitted or absorbed only when an electron jumps from one non-radiating orbit to another.
Choose the correct option:
options: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
explanation: Both statements are Bohr's fundamental quantum postulates: L = mvr = n h/(2π), and ΔE = E_initial - E_final = hν.

subject: Physics
questionText:
Consider the following statements regarding hydrogen atom energy states:
Statement I: The total energy of an electron in a bound Bohr orbit is negative.
Statement II: The kinetic energy of the electron in any Bohr orbit equals the magnitude of its total energy (K = |E|).
Choose the correct option:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
explanation: Both statements are correct. By the Virial theorem for Coulomb potential: U = -2K, so Total Energy E = K + U = -K. Hence K = |E| and U = 2E = -2K.

subject: Physics
questionText:
Consider the following statements regarding nuclear stability:
Statement I: For stable light nuclei (A < 20), the neutron to proton ratio (N/Z) is approximately 1.
Statement II: Heavy stable nuclei require more protons than neutrons (Z > N) to overcome nuclear forces.
Choose the correct option:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
explanation: Statement I is correct. Statement II is incorrect because heavy nuclei require excess neutrons (N > Z, ratio ~1.5) to provide additional attractive strong nuclear force without adding disruptive Coulomb repulsion.

subject: Physics
questionText:
Consider the following statements regarding radioactive decay:
Statement I: The rate of disintegration (-dN/dt) of a radioactive sample is directly proportional to the number of active nuclei N present at that instant.
Statement II: The radioactive decay constant λ depends strongly on external physical conditions such as temperature and pressure.
Choose the correct option:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
explanation: Statement I is Rutherford-Soddy law. Statement II is incorrect because nuclear decay is an internal spontaneous nuclear process unaffected by temperature, pressure, or chemical state.

subject: Physics
questionText:
Consider the following statements regarding mass defect and binding energy:
Statement I: The mass of any stable nucleus is strictly less than the sum of the masses of its individual separated nucleons.
Statement II: 1 atomic mass unit (1 u) is equivalent to approximately 931.5 MeV of energy.
Choose the correct option:
options: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
explanation: Both statements are correct. The mass deficit Δm = Σm_nucleons - M_nucleus is converted into binding energy according to E = Δm c² (1 u = 931.5 MeV).

subject: Physics
questionText:
Statement I: In any Bohr orbit of a hydrogen atom, the kinetic energy K, potential energy U, and total energy E are related by K = -E and U = 2E = -2K.
Statement II: As an electron jumps from a lower orbit (n = 1) to a higher orbit (n = 2), its total energy E and potential energy U increase (become less negative), while its kinetic energy K decreases.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
explanation: In n=1: E = -13.6 eV, K = +13.6 eV, U = -27.2 eV. In n=2: E = -3.4 eV, K = +3.4 eV, U = -6.8 eV. Both statements are correct.

subject: Physics
questionText:
Statement I: When an electron in an excited state n of a collection of Hydrogen atoms de-excites to the ground state (n = 1), the maximum number of distinct spectral lines emitted is n(n - 1) / 2.
Statement II: The shortest wavelength (highest energy photon) in the Balmer series corresponds to the series limit transition from n₂ = ∞ to n₁ = 2.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
explanation: Number of lines is nC₂ = n(n-1)/2; shortest wavelength in any series corresponds to n₂ = ∞.

subject: Physics
questionText:
Statement I: According to de Broglie's explanation of Bohr's quantization condition, a bound electron orbit of radius r_n is stable only if its circumference contains an integral number of de Broglie wavelengths (2π r_n = n λ).
Statement II: Substituting λ = h / (m v_n) into 2π r_n = n λ immediately yields Bohr's angular momentum quantization condition L = m v_n r_n = n h / (2π).
options: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
explanation: Standing matter-wave condition 2πr = n(h/mv) directly gives mvr = nh/(2π).

subject: Physics
questionText:
Statement I: The strong nuclear force is a short-range force that is strongly attractive at nucleon separations of ~1 to 2 fm, becomes negligible beyond ~3 fm, and becomes strongly repulsive at separations less than 0.8 fm.
Statement II: The repulsive core of the nuclear force at distances < 0.8 fm prevents the nucleus from collapsing to a point and maintains constant nuclear density.
options: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
explanation: Both statements accurately describe the potential energy curve of the nucleon-nucleon force.

subject: Physics
questionText:
Statement I: In a nuclear fission reactor, heavy water (D₂O) or graphite is used as a moderator to slow down fast neutrons to thermal energies, while Cadmium or Boron rods are used as control rods to absorb excess neutrons.
Statement II: Thermal neutrons (~0.025 eV) have a much higher probability (cross-section) of inducing fission in ²³⁵₉₂U than fast neutrons.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
explanation: Both statements are key NCERT nuclear reactor principles.

questionText: Mass defect (Δm) during a nuclear fusion reaction is 0.01 amu. Energy released is approximately: (1 amu = 931.5 MeV)

subject: Physics
questionText: The radius of the first orbit of hydrogen atom is 0.53 Å (0.053 nm). The radius of the third orbit (n = 3) of Li²⁺ ion is:
explanation: Bohr radius formula: r_n = r₁ × (n² / Z). For Li²⁺, Z = 3, n = 3. So r₃ = 0.53 × (3² / 3) = 0.53 × 3 = 1.59 Å.

subject: Physics
questionText: What is the energy required to excite an electron from the ground state (n = 1) to the first excited state (n = 2) in a hydrogen atom?
explanation: E_n = -13.6 / n² eV. E₁ = -13.6 eV, E₂ = -13.6 / 4 = -3.4 eV. Excitation energy ΔE = E₂ - E₁ = -3.4 - (-13.6) = 10.2 eV.

subject: Physics
questionText: If the half-life of a radioactive isotope is 5 days, what fraction of the original active nuclei will remain undecayed after 20 days?
explanation: Number of half-lives n = t / T_1/2 = 20 / 5 = 4. Remaining fraction = (1/2)ⁿ = (1/2)⁴ = 1/16 ≈ 6.25%.

subject: Physics
questionText: The ratio of the radii of two nuclei with mass numbers 27 and 64 respectively is:
explanation: Nuclear radius R = R₀ A^(1/3). Therefore R₁ / R₂ = (A₁ / A₂)^(1/3) = (27 / 64)^(1/3) = 3 / 4.

subject: Physics
questionText: The binding energy per nucleon of ⁴₂He is 7.0 MeV and that of ²₁H (deuterium) is 1.1 MeV. In the fusion reaction ²₁H + ²₁H → ⁴₂He + Q, the energy Q released is:
explanation: Total BE of products = BE(⁴₂He) = 4 × 7.0 = 28.0 MeV. Total BE of reactants = 2 × [2 × 1.1] = 4.4 MeV. Energy released Q = 28.0 - 4.4 = 23.6 MeV.

subject: Physics
questionText: In the Hydrogen atom, the radius of the first Bohr orbit (n = 1) is 0.53 Å. What is the radius of the third Bohr orbit (n = 3) of the Hydrogen atom?
explanation: Since r_n = n² r₁ for Hydrogen (Z = 1), r₃ = 3² × 0.53 Å = 9 × 0.53 Å = 4.77 Å.

subject: Physics
questionText: The ionization energy of a Hydrogen atom in its ground state is 13.6 eV. The energy required to excite the electron from the first excited state (n = 2) to the second excited state (n = 3) is:
explanation: First excited state is n = 2 (E₂ = -13.6/4 = -3.40 eV); second excited state is n = 3 (E₃ = -13.6/9 = -1.51 eV). ΔE = E₃ - E₂ = -1.51 - (-3.40) = 1.89 eV.

subject: Physics
questionText: What is the ratio of the longest wavelength to the shortest wavelength in the Lyman series of the Hydrogen spectrum?
explanation: For Lyman series (n₁ = 1): longest λ is for n₂ = 2 => 1/λ_max = R(1 - 1/4) = 3R/4 => λ_max = 4/(3R). Shortest λ is for n₂ = ∞ => 1/λ_min = R(1 - 0) => λ_min = 1/R. Ratio λ_max / λ_min = 4 : 3.

subject: Physics
questionText: Two nuclei have mass numbers in the ratio 8 : 27. The ratio of their nuclear radii (R₁ : R₂) and the ratio of their nuclear mass densities (ρ₁ : ρ₂) are respectively:
explanation: R ∝ A^(1/3) => R₁ / R₂ = (8 / 27)^(1/3) = 2 : 3. Nuclear mass density is independent of A, so ρ₁ : ρ₂ = 1 : 1.

subject: Physics
questionText: A radioactive sample has a half-life of 5 days. What percentage of the initial sample will have DECAYED after 20 days?
explanation: Number of half-lives n = 20 / 5 = 4. Undecayed fraction N / N₀ = (1/2)⁴ = 1/16 = 6.25%. Therefore, DECAYED percentage = 100% - 6.25% = 93.75%.

subject: Physics
questionText: A radioactive nucleus ²³⁸₉₂U undergoes a series of decays emitting 3 alpha (α) particles and 2 beta-minus (β⁻) particles. The atomic number (Z) and mass number (A) of the resulting daughter nucleus are:
explanation: Each α removes (ΔA = 4, ΔZ = 2); each β⁻ adds ΔZ = +1. Thus A' = 238 - 3(4) = 226, and Z' = 92 - 3(2) + 2(1) = 92 - 6 + 2 = 88.

subject: Physics
questionText: If the binding energy per nucleon of a Deuteron (²₁H) is 1.1 MeV and that of a Helium nucleus (⁴₂He) is 7.0 MeV, the total energy released when two deuterons fuse to form one Helium nucleus (²₁H + ²₁H → ⁴₂He) is:
explanation: Total BE of reactants = 2 × (2 × 1.1 MeV) = 4.4 MeV. Total BE of product ⁴₂He = 4 × 7.0 MeV = 28.0 MeV. Energy released Q = BE_products - BE_reactants = 28.0 - 4.4 = 23.6 MeV.

subject: Physics
questionText: In a Bohr Hydrogen atom, an electron transitions from the n = 4 energy level to the ground state (n = 1). How many different spectral wavelengths can be emitted by a gas of such excited atoms?
explanation: Number of possible spectral lines = n(n - 1) / 2 = 4(3) / 2 = 6.

subject: Physics
questionText: Shortest wavelength in Lyman series of Hydrogen spectrum is: (R = 1.097 × 10⁷ m⁻¹)
explanation: For shortest wavelength in Lyman series n1 = 1, n2 = ∞. 1/λ = R (1/1² - 0) = R => λ = 1/R ≈ 91.2 nm.

subject: Physics
questionText: Ionization potential of Hydrogen atom is 13.6 V. Energy required to excite electron from ground state to first excited state is:

subject: Physics
questionText: In a ballistic nuclear decay, a stationary nucleus of mass number A = 220 spontaneously emits an alpha particle (mass number = 4) with kinetic energy K_alpha = 5.4 MeV. What is the recoil kinetic energy of the daughter nucleus (mass number = 216), and what is the total disintegration energy (Q-value) of the alpha decay?
options: Recoil KE of daughter = 5.40 MeV; Total Q-value = 10.80 MeV
Recoil KE of daughter = 0.10 MeV; Total Q-value = 5.50 MeV
Recoil KE of daughter = 0.20 MeV; Total Q-value = 5.60 MeV
Recoil KE of daughter = 0.05 MeV; Total Q-value = 5.45 MeV
explanation: By conservation of linear momentum (0 = p_alpha - p_d => p_d = p_alpha), kinetic energy (K = p^2 / 2m) is inversely proportional to mass: K_d / K_alpha = m_alpha / m_d = 4 / 216 = 1 / 54. Thus Recoil KE of daughter K_d = 5.4 MeV / 54 = 0.10 MeV. Total Q-value = K_alpha + K_d = 5.40 + 0.10 = 5.50 MeV.

subject: Physics
questionText: Bohr's model postulates that electron moves in orbits where angular momentum is:
explanation: Bohr: mvr = nh/2π — angular momentum is integral multiple of h/2π.

subject: Physics
questionText: Half-life of a radioactive substance is:

subject: Physics
questionText: Radius of a nucleus (R) of mass number A is given by:

subject: Physics
questionText: Nuclear density is independent of mass number A and has a constant value of approximately:
explanation: Nuclear density ρ = Mass / Volume = (m A) / (4/3 π R0³ A) = 3m / (4π R0³) ≈ 2.3 × 10¹⁷ kg/m³.

subject: Physics
questionText: Mass defect (Δm) and Nuclear Binding Energy (E_b) for a nucleus of Z protons and N neutrons (mass M_nucleus) is:
options: E_b = Δm · c^2 = [Z m_p + (A - Z) m_n - M_nucleus] × 931.5 MeV
explanation: 1 unified atomic mass unit (1 u) mass defect is equivalent to 931.5 MeV of nuclear binding energy.

subject: Physics
questionText: The Binding Energy per Nucleon (E_b / A) curve has a broad maximum of approximately 8.75 MeV/nucleon for:

explanation: ⁵⁶Fe has the highest binding energy per nucleon (8.75 MeV), making it the most stable nuclear species.

subject: Physics
questionText: Nuclear Fission of Uranium-235 (235_92U + 1_0n -> 144_56Ba + 89_36Kr + 3 1_0n + Q) releases approximately how much energy per fission event?
explanation: Each U-235 fission event releases ~200 MeV (mostly kinetic energy of fission fragments).

subject: Physics
questionText: Nuclear Fusion in the Sun's core (Proton-Proton Cycle: 4 1_1H -> 4_2He + 2 e+ + 2 ν + 26.7 MeV) requires extreme temperatures (>10^7 K) to:
options: Overcome the strong electrostatic Coulomb repulsion between positively charged protons
explanation: High thermal kinetic energy at >10⁷ K allows colliding protons to overcome the Coulomb barrier and enter short-range strong nuclear attraction.

subject: Physics
questionText: Radioactive Decay Law states that rate of disintegration (-dN/dt) is proportional to active nuclei N present at that instant:
options: N(t) = N0 e^(-λt) [where λ is decay constant]
explanation: -dN/dt = λ N => N(t) = N0 e^(-λt).

subject: Physics
questionText: Relation between Half-life (T_1/2) and Decay Constant (λ) is:
options: T_1/2 = ln 2 / λ = 0.693 / λ (and Mean Life τ = 1 / λ = 1.44 T_1/2)
explanation: T_1/2 = 0.693/λ. Average/mean lifetime τ = 1/λ = T_1/2 / 0.693 = 1.44 T_1/2.

subject: Physics
questionText: The SI unit of Radioactivity (decay activity A = λN) is:
options: Becquerel (1 Bq = 1 decay per second; 1 Curie = 3.7 × 10^10 Bq; 1 Rutherford = 10^6 Bq)
explanation: 1 Becquerel (Bq) = 1 disintegration per second. 1 Ci = 3.7 × 10¹⁰ Bq.

subject: Physics
questionText: Impact parameter (b) in Rutherford α-particle scattering is the perpendicular distance of the initial velocity vector from the nucleus. For a head-on collision (scattering angle θ = 180°):
options: b = 0 (Distance of closest approach is minimum, r0 = 2k Z e^2 / K)
explanation: b = [k Z e² cot(θ/2)] / K. For θ = 180°, cot(90°) = 0, so impact parameter b = 0.

subject: Physics
questionText: An α-particle of kinetic energy K is fired head-on towards a gold nucleus (Z = 79). The distance of closest approach (r0) is proportional to:
explanation: At turning point, entire kinetic energy converts to electrostatic potential energy: K = k(2e)(Ze) / r0 => r0 = 2k Z e² / K.

subject: Physics
questionText: The shortest wavelength (series limit, n2 = ∞) in the Balmer series of hydrogen spectrum is:
options: 4 / R ≈ 364.6 nm (where R is Rydberg constant)

subject: Physics
questionText: The Strong Nuclear Force that binds protons and neutrons inside a nucleus is:

questionText: In Alpha (α) decay (A_Z X -> (A-4)_(Z-2) Y + 4_2He):

No change in A and Z

questionText: In Beta-minus (β-) decay (A_Z X -> A_(Z+1) Y + e- + ν̅):

explanation: n -> p + e⁻ + ν̅. Mass number A is unchanged, atomic number Z increases by 1, accompanied by an antineutrino.

subject: Physics
questionText: In Beta-plus (β+) decay (A_Z X -> A_(Z-1) Y + e+ + ν):

questionText: Moderators used in nuclear fission reactors to slow down fast neutrons (from ~2 MeV to ~0.025 eV thermal neutrons) are:

questionText: Coolants used to carry away enormous fission heat from a nuclear reactor core to steam generators include:

subject: Physics
questionText: Pair Production (γ -> e- + e+) is the creation of an electron and a positron from a high-energy gamma photon in the Coulomb field of a nucleus. The minimum threshold photon energy required is:

questionText: The half-life of a radioactive sample is 10 min. Starting with 1000 nuclei, how many will remain after 20 min?

explanation: Number of half-lives n = 60 / 20 = 3. Remaining fraction = (1/2)^3 = 1/8.

questionText: In Rutherford's alpha-particle scattering experiment, for a head-on collision (impact parameter b = 0, scattering angle θ = 180°), the distance of closest approach d₀ is inversely proportional to:

questionText: Which of the following nuclei has the HIGHEST binding energy per nucleon (~8.75 MeV), making it one of the most stable nuclides in nature?

subject: Physics
questionText: In a photoelectric experiment, if the slope of the stopping potential (V0) versus incident frequency (nu) graph is measured to be 'S', which fundamental constant can be directly calculated as e × S?
explanation: Einstein's photoelectric equation: e × V0 = h × nu - phi => V0 = (h / e) × nu - (phi / e). Comparing with y = m x + c, the slope is S = h / e. Therefore, h = e × S (Planck's constant).

subject: Physics
questionText: The de Broglie wavelengths of an alpha particle and a proton accelerated from rest through the same electrostatic potential difference V are in the ratio (lambda_alpha : lambda_p):
explanation: de Broglie wavelength lambda = h / sqrt(2 × m × q × V). Therefore, lambda_alpha / lambda_p = sqrt((m_p × q_p) / (m_alpha × q_alpha)). Since m_alpha = 4 m_p and q_alpha = 2 q_p, the ratio is sqrt((1 × 1) / (4 × 2)) = sqrt(1/8) = 1 / (2 × sqrt(2)).

subject: Physics
questionText: A proton, a deuteron, and an alpha particle, all having the SAME kinetic energy K, enter a uniform magnetic field B perpendicular to their velocities. What is the ratio of the radii of their circular paths (r_p : r_d : r_alpha) and the ratio of their time periods of revolution (T_p : T_d : T_alpha)?
options: Radii ratio = 1 : sqrt(2) : 2; Time periods ratio = 1 : 2 : 4
Radii ratio = 1 : sqrt(2) : 1; Time periods ratio = 1 : 2 : 2
Radii ratio = sqrt(2) : 1 : 1; Time periods ratio = 2 : 1 : 1
explanation: 1) For equal kinetic energy K, radius r = sqrt(2 m K) / (q B), so r is proportional to sqrt(m) / q. Using m_p : m_d : m_alpha = 1 : 2 : 4 and q_p : q_d : q_alpha = 1 : 1 : 2, we get r_p : r_d : r_alpha = (sqrt(1)/1) : (sqrt(2)/1) : (sqrt(4)/2) = 1 : sqrt(2) : 1! (Proton and alpha particle have the exact same radius!). 2) Time period T = 2 pi m / (q B) is proportional to (m / q): T_p : T_d : T_alpha = (1/1) : (2/1) : (4/2) = 1 : 2 : 2.

subject: Physics
questionText: A thermodynamic system of 1 mole of an ideal monoatomic gas is taken around a clockwise rectangular cycle ABCDA on a P-V diagram, bounded by pressures P0 and 3P0, and volumes V0 and 2V0 (A = (V0, P0) -> B = (V0, 3P0) -> C = (2V0, 3P0) -> D = (2V0, P0) -> A). Find the net work done by the gas per cycle (W_cycle), the total heat absorbed during the heating stages A -> B -> C (Q_in), and the thermal efficiency (eta = W_cycle / Q_in) of this cycle:
options: W_cycle = 2 P0 V0; Q_in = 7.5 P0 V0; Efficiency eta = 26.7%
W_cycle = 2 P0 V0; Q_in = 6 P0 V0; Efficiency eta = 33.3%
W_cycle = 3 P0 V0; Q_in = 10.5 P0 V0; Efficiency eta = 28.6%
W_cycle = 2 P0 V0; Q_in = (21 / 2) P0 V0 (= 10.5 P0 V0); Efficiency eta = 4 / 21 (≈ 19.05%)
explanation: 1) Net work per clockwise cycle = Area of rectangle = (3P0 - P0)(2V0 - V0) = 2 P0 V0. 2) Heat is absorbed ONLY during A -> B (isochoric heating at V0 from P0 to 3P0) and B -> C (isobaric expansion at 3P0 from V0 to 2V0): For monoatomic gas (Cv = 3R/2, Cp = 5R/2), Q_AB = n Cv Delta T = (3/2) V0 (3P0 - P0) = 3 P0 V0; and Q_BC = n Cp Delta T = (5/2) (3P0)(2V0 - V0) = (15/2) P0 V0 = 7.5 P0 V0. Total heat absorbed Q_in = Q_AB + Q_BC = 3 + 7.5 = (21 / 2) P0 V0! 3) Efficiency eta = W_cycle / Q_in = 2 / (21/2) = 4 / 21 ≈ 19.05%.

subject: Physics
questionText:
Match the semiconductor types and materials in Column I with their distinguishing properties in Column II:
Column I:
(A) Intrinsic Semiconductor
(B) n-type Semiconductor
(C) p-type Semiconductor
(D) Elemental Semiconductors
Column II:
(1) Pure crystal where electron concentration equals hole concentration (n_e = n_h = n_i)
(2) Doped with pentavalent impurities (P, As, Sb); majority carriers are electrons (n_e ≫ n_h)
(3) Doped with trivalent impurities (B, Al, In); majority carriers are holes (n_h ≫ n_e)
(4) Silicon (Si, E_g ≈ 1.1 eV) and Germanium (Ge, E_g ≈ 0.7 eV)
explanation: Intrinsic has n_e = n_h; pentavalent donor doping gives n-type (n_e ≫ n_h); trivalent acceptor doping gives p-type (n_h ≫ n_e); Si and Ge are group 14 elemental semiconductors.

questionText:

(2) Heavily forward-biased (emits photons on spontaneous electron-hole recombination)
(3) Reverse-biased (detects optical signals via change in reverse saturation current)
(4) Reverse-breakdown region (maintains constant breakdown voltage)
explanation: Solar cells operate without external bias; LEDs are forward biased; photodiodes are reverse biased for quick response; Zener diodes operate in reverse breakdown.

questionText:
